question: In the present digital age, social media has revolutionised our way of communication and interaction. However, it has raised several ethical issues and challenges. Describe the key ethical dilemmas in this regard.

“Constitutional morality is not a natural sentiment but a product of civil education and adherence to the rule of law.” Examine the significance of constitutional morality for public servants, highlighting its role in promoting good governance and ensuring accountability in public administration.
Carl von Clausewitz once said, “War is a diplomacy by other means.” Critically analyse the above statement in the present context of contemporary geo-political conflict.

Keeping the national security in mind, examine the ethical dilemmas related to controversies over environmental clearance of development projects in ecologically sensitive border areas in the country.
“Those who in trouble untroubled are, Will trouble trouble itself.” – Thiruvalluvar. What does this quotation convey to you in the present context?
“The greatest discovery of my generation is that a human being can alter his life by altering his attitudes.” – William James. What does this quotation convey to you in the present context?
“The strength of a society is not in its laws, but in the morality of its people.” – Swami Vivekananda. What does this quotation convey to you in the present context?

“For any kind of social re-engineering by successfully implementing welfare schemes, a civil servant must use reason and critical thinking in an ethical framework.” Justify this statement with suitable examples.
What are the major teachings of Mahavir? Explain their relevance in the contemporary world.
“One who is devoted to one’s duty attains highest perfection in life.” Analyse this statement with reference to sense of responsibility and personal fulfilment as a civil servant.
To achieve holistic development, a civil servant acts as an enabler and active facilitator of growth rather than a regulator. What specific measures will you suggest to achieve this goal?

It is said that for an ethical work culture, there must be a code of ethics in place in every organisation. To ensure value-based and compliance-based work culture, what suitable measures would you adopt in your workplace?

India is an emerging economic power of the world as it has recently secured the status of fourth largest economy of the world as per IMF projection. However, it has been observed that in some sectors, allocated funds remain either under-utilised or misutilised. What specific measures would you recommend for ensuring accountability and proper utilisation of public funds?

Vijay was Deputy Commissioner of a remote district of a hilly Northern State. Heavy rains and a cloudburst caused extensive damage; roads and telecommunications were disrupted, more than 200 people were killed and about 5000 injured. Vijay’s mother in Kerala then died, while the district emergency deteriorated and he was urged to return for the last rites. (a) What options are available with Vijay? (b) What ethical dilemmas is he facing? (c) Critically evaluate each option. (d) Which option is most appropriate and why?

A district administration proposes clearing a portion of ecologically sensitive forest land for housing homeless and economically weaker sections. The forest provides biodiversity, climate regulation, soil protection and tribal/nomadic livelihoods, while the administration cites welfare, human rights, wildlife conflict and law-and-order concerns. (a) Can deforestation be ethically justified for housing? (b) What socio-economic, administrative and ethical challenges arise? (c) What alternatives or policy interventions can protect both environmental integrity and human dignity?

Subash, Secretary PWD, is handling a proposed mega road project. His son wants the exact location to buy land before prices rise, while the PWD Minister pressures Subash to advance the project for his nephew’s infrastructure business. (a) Discuss the ethical issues. (b) Critically examine the options. (c) Which is most appropriate and why?

Rajesh, an Administrative Officer in a public-sector undertaking, is seeking promotion and is pressured by his reporting officer to procure stationery from a particular vendor. The proposed purchase exceeds the delegated financial limit, and splitting the expenditure into smaller orders is a common but rule-violating practice. (a) What options are available? (b) What ethical issues are involved? (c) Which option is most appropriate and why?

You are appointed Administrator In-charge of a district to monitor MGNREGA. You discover non-payment to actual workers, defective muster rolls, mismatches between work and payments, fictitious beneficiaries, improper job cards, siphoning of funds and approved works that never existed. (a) What is your reaction and how would you restore proper functioning? (b) What actions would you initiate? (c) How would you deal with the situation?

Ashok is Divisional Commissioner in a North-Eastern border district. A neighbouring country is in civil war; 200–250 civilians, mainly women and children, seek to cross the border, accompanied by about 10 armed soldiers in uniform. Some are injured and Ashok cannot reach the Home Secretary. (a) What options are available? (b) What ethical and legal dilemmas arise? (c) Which option is appropriate and why? (d) What extra precautions should border police take regarding soldiers in uniform?
